keyVerseText: And Moses said unto Joshua, Choose us out men, and go out, fight with Amalek: to morrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the rod of God in mine hand. Joshua: called Jesus
rootMeaning: The name יְהוֹשׁוּעַ (Yᵉhôwshûwaʻ) originates from a combination of two Hebrew elements: יְהֹוָה (Yᵉhôvâh), the proper name of God meaning 'the existing One,' and the root יָשַׁע, meaning 'to save.' Thus, the literal meaning of the name is 'Jehovah is salvation' or 'the Lord saves.' This etymology highlights a divine attribute of God as the ultimate source of salvation, which goes beyond the English name Joshua by embedding God’s saving power directly into the identity of the person bearing the name.
usageInScripture: The word יְהוֹשׁוּעַ appears 218 times in Scripture, predominantly translated as 'Joshua' or phrases like 'And Joshua' and 'unto Joshua.' This consistent translation emphasizes the personal name of a key biblical figure, Moses’ successor and leader of Israel, underscoring his role in God’s redemptive plan. The frequency and variety of the phraseology indicate that Joshua is central in narrative contexts involving leadership, conquest, and covenant faithfulness, reflecting his importance in Israel’s history.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding יְהוֹשׁוּעַ as 'Jehovah is salvation' enriches the Christian faith by pointing to the person and work of Jesus Christ, whose name in Hebrew is a later form of the same root. This connection reveals a continuity between the Old Testament figure who led God’s people into the Promised Land and the New Testament Savior who leads believers into eternal salvation. The name encapsulates the truth that salvation is found in God alone, and it invites believers to trust in His power to save. Recognizing this name’s meaning helps Christians appreciate the divine initiative in salvation history and God’s faithfulness to His promises.
keyVerseReflection: Exodus 17:9 states, 'And Moses said unto Joshua, Choose us out men, and go out, fight with Amalek: to morrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the rod of God in mine hand.' Here, the name Joshua signifies more than a leader; it embodies the divine assurance of salvation and victory through God’s power. Moses’ instruction to Joshua to lead the battle is a moment where the name’s meaning—'Jehovah is salvation'—is put into action, as Joshua becomes the instrument of God’s saving deliverance for Israel. This verse thus highlights Joshua’s role as God’s chosen agent in fulfilling His saving purposes.
